title: Relative nonpositivity of the supported integral-image Koszul complex
statement:
Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use the small étale and pro-étale sites in a common indexing universe [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its norm-topological valuation ring $B=\mathcal O_E$, and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On every scheme $T$ put $B_T=p_T^*C(-,B)$ and use internal $B_T$-module objects [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $S=T_r\xrightarrow{a_r}\cdots\xrightarrow{a_1}T_0=X$ be any finite chain whose arrows are quasi-compact open immersions or closed immersions with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Set $J=J_1\circ\cdots\circ J_r$, where $J_t=(a_t)_!$ for an open arrow and $J_t=(a_t)_*$ for a closed arrow [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]; for $r=0$ set $J=\mathrm{id}$. Assume that the source $S$ of the chain is Noetherian, meaning quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $f:L	o M$ be any morphism of internal $B_S$-modules such that, separately on some pro-étale covering for each of $L,M$, the module is $B_S\otimes_{\underline B_S}\underline P$ for a finitely presented abstract $B$-module $P$ (a cokernel of a map between finite free modules); these are the finite scalar local models of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Take the actual abelian image $I=\operatorname{im}f$, with no topological closure. For any affine pro-étale object $v:U	o X$ [sk-def-pe-morphisms], put $N=v^*J(I)$ using module pullback [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. Let $n\ge1$ and let $C_n(N)$ be the complex of underlying abelian sheaves on $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $N$ in degrees $-1,0$, differential $\pi^n:N	o N$, and zero elsewhere. For the comparison morphism $
u_U:U_{\mathrm{proét}}	o U_{\mathrm{ét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the ordinary derived abelian direct image satisfies
$$R
u_{U,*}C_n(N)\in D^{\le0}(\operatorname{Ab}(U_{\mathrm{ét}})),\qquad\mathcal H^q(R
u_{U,*}C_n(N))=0\quad(q>0).$$
Derived categories are ordinary localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No cohomological-dimension bound on $X$ or its étale objects is assumed. No classicality, derived completeness, locally constant rank, or locally constant elementary-divisor type of $I$ or of its reductions is assumed. Empty schemes, empty chains and zero maps are included.

source.place: WANTED: an independent proof/reference for this local relative-comparison theorem for arbitrary supported finite-scalar-model images. Section 8, condition (8.1), and Lemma 8.6 motivate the global application, but do not state this local theorem. Agent-created prerequisite, not a quotation of Lemma 8.6 or of classical comparison.

proof.text: The source-image classicality theorem gives etale antecedents for all homology sheaves of C_n(image f). Apply preservation along the actual support path and the actual module pullback to get classical abelian homology of C_n(N).

The literal double complex has zero terms below -1 and above 0, by HomologicalComplex.isZero_double_X. Hence its derived image is in D^{>=-1} and D^{<=0}. Regard it as a D+ object and transport the classicality witnesses across homologyFunctorFactors.

Apply the bounded classical abelian counit. For q>0 the homology of C_n(N) is zero by its upper bound. Mapping the counit isomorphism by H^q gives zero homology of nu^* Rnu_* C_n(N). Exact faithful inverse image reflects zero homology, using isZero_homologyFunctor_of_isZero_homologyFunctor_mapDerivedCategory_obj. Membership in D^{<=0} follows by DerivedCategory.isLE_iff.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q09-c3d89c88c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the report, every cited statement, the only citer lem-sfb-supported-image-torsion-reductions-cd, and HRS Theorem 6.2 and Remark 6.4 in the local PDF; coord/dag-sync.md is not in the snapshot. The delivery has no new nodes. Its only statement change from the base is the added hypothesis that the source S is Noetherian; the new stmt_deps (quasi-compact scheme, locally Noetherian) are exactly what that sentence uses, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. I checked the counterexample to the old unrestricted statement myself and it holds. On Spec of the eventually-constant Q-sequences (points N ∪ {∞}), take multiplication by a=(2^m,0) on free B=Z_2 with n=1. The image is torsion-free, so C_1(I) is I/2I. On w-contractible V, extremal disconnectedness gives I/2I = j_*F_2, so Rν_* C_1 = Rj_et,* F_2. R^1j_et,*F_2 is nonzero at ∞ via the quadratic characters Q(√p_m): each finite K kills only finitely many of them. So the old statement is false (E7, reported under Source error with statement_correction and the citer marked holds:false). The Noetherian repair is minimal and matches HRS 6.2(3) and Remark 6.4. Steps: (1) the Noetherian constructible-heart theorem with Λ=O_E makes I = ker(M→coker f) constructible; this is the only use of Noetherianity. (2) S is qcqs; the finite-model quotient theorem (qcqs only) puts cohomology in [-1,0] and makes it constructible; the cone calculus identifies the reduction with [I→π^n I]; constructible comparison over the discrete Noetherian B/π^n gives classicality. (3) Open arrows use the finite-ring j_! comparison. Closed immersions are qcqs, so direct-image comparison applies in degree 0. j_! and i_* are exact under the chain hypothesis, and operations transport identifies the internal and sectionwise functors. (4) v^* is exact and the pullback square needs no qcqs on v, so H^t C_n(N) ≅ v^*J H^t C_n(I) are classical. (5) The bounded-below unit and the classical derived equivalence give the counit iso; ν^* is exact and faithful, so positive Rν_* cohomology vanishes. (6) Edge cases checked: empty scheme and chain, zero map, identity over a field. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact (reached via the zl dualizable-model chain) is the generic exactness of geometric-morphism inverse images. It is neither a step of the trace formula nor of Poincaré duality, and the HRS constructible heart is outside both assumptions, so I accept it. The declared tool_uses are generic and accepted. No fixes. Maintainer: record the source error in HUMAN.md and reopen lem-sfb-supported-image-torsion-reductions-cd, whose step 5 used the unrestricted form for arbitrary S. Its own integral claim is not refuted by this example; only its route through this lemma fails.
